conclusion.justification: The report explicitly rejects the claim, stating that the assertion that influenza vaccination causes Alzheimer's disease is unsupported by scientific evidence, debunked, and contradicted by studies showing a protective effect instead.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**The claim that influenza vaccination causes Alzheimer's disease is not supported by scientific evidence — the actual research shows the opposite.**

The claim traces back largely to statements by Hugh Fudenberg, an immunologist whose unsubstantiated assertion that repeated flu vaccination raises Alzheimer's risk tenfold (attributed to mercury/aluminum content) has been repeatedly debunked as lacking peer-reviewed support (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/flu-shot-avoidance/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._Hugh_Fudenberg).

By contrast, multiple peer-reviewed studies point toward a **protective**, not causal, relationship. A large retrospective cohort study found that adults 65+ who received at least one flu vaccine had a 40% lower risk of developing Alzheimer's disease compared to unvaccinated peers (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9484126/). A more recent study comparing high-dose versus standard-dose flu vaccines found high-dose vaccination was associated with a further reduced risk of Alzheimer's dementia in adults over 65, with a stronger effect in women (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782). Additional research summarized by the Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation states there is "no peer-reviewed scientific evidence" supporting the causal claim, and instead evidence supports a protective association (https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot).

**Conclusion:** The weight of scientific evidence contradicts the idea that flu vaccination causes Alzheimer's disease. Instead, credible cohort studies consistently find flu vaccination is associated with a *reduced* risk of Alzheimer's and dementia, likely due to reduced systemic infection/inflammation burden in older adults. The "causes Alzheimer's" claim appears to originate from an unverified assertion by a single discredited source rather than rigorous research.
